prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Top Scandinavian interiors magazine: a Copenhagen living room, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp. Hero at first glance: the three prints over the sofa, right third.

2. LIGHT. One key: soft north daylight from the left window, no sun; outside, bare birches, no snow, no buildings. Exposed for white: the back wall by the corner clean white, a step under the glowing reveals; the glass brightest, detailed. The back wall falls off smoothly half a stop to the right edge; window wall in soft shade. Every piece: a lit window face, a shadow side a stop darker; armchair and table cast long soft shadows right and toward the camera; dense contact shadows. Ceiling a touch darker, darkest top right. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, pink or grey. Lamps 2700 K, low, shadowless: a warm pool from the wall lamp on the armchair, a softer one from the pendant on the bare table centre; short soft fans up and down from the travertine cubes.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC, faint chalky movement. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. SOFA, fixed, 220 cm: exactly the clay's block, arms at x 0.52 and 0.84, as reference 1, never wider; slubby oatmeal cotton-linen #E6DCCB, tapered oak legs. Table and armchair frame: oiled oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft highlight on the table top. Armchair: mist-grey wool boucle.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
a. ART, x 0.60-0.79, y 0.28-0.51: three 50 x 70 prints, minimal oatmeal, sand and charcoal shapes on off-white, thin light-oak frames, the wall's strongest contrast.
b. TRAVERTINE CUBES at x 0.57 and 0.83: two hand-sized cubes of warm honed travertine, open pores, light washing out of top and bottom.
c. PENDANT, x 0.60-0.67, y 0.05-0.17: a flat ribbed warm-white silk lantern, thin black rod, bare wall below it.
d. CURTAINS: sheer natural linen-blend, S-fold, slim black rod, backlit, hems on the floor.
e. VASE on the sill, x 0.31-0.35: a 31 cm cream distressed clay jar, 3-4 eucalyptus stems.
f. WALL LAMP, plate x 0.12, y 0.37: matte black swing arm, tapered warm-white fabric shade; a short cord down into the flush socket at y 0.43; bare wall below.
g. BASKET, x 0.86-0.92, y 0.67-0.80: empty seagrass belly basket.
h. RUG under table and front legs: 230 x 330 white hand-woven flat wool, tone-on-tone diamond weave, fine grey flecks.
i. CUSHION, sofa left: 50 cm warm-white boucle, tight loops.
j. CUSHION in front of it: 45 cm sage chenille knit.
k. LUMBAR, right seat: 30 x 50 charcoal linen-look.
l. THROW over the right arm: thin crinkled cream cotton muslin, short frayed fringe.
m. RUNNER on the table's left third: sage-grey linen-look, fringed ends.
n. CANDLE HOLDERS right of the table centre: two hand-sized travertine pedestals, unlit candles 15 and 10 cm.
o. BOWL beside them: 21 cm warm-white matte belly bowl, empty.

5. NOT IN FRAME: floor lamp, wall decor, plant, pouf, magazines, books, mirror, any cable on wall or floor, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.

exposure.flag: DARK: needs more than +0.2 stop, not lifted further

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6 (the Bible grade): WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

clay_lock.method: regions = whole frame, quadrants, ceiling/floor bands and the clay boxes of fixed furniture / windows / openings; peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable (weak texture), so the verdict is visual (<aid>-lock.png) with the strong-peak number as support

verdict.visual: BROKE: sofa about 1.22-1.28x the clay width (arms ~0.49/0.87 vs 0.52/0.84), armchair shifted left, window and sconce shifted

sofa_width_check.method: strongest vertical edge within +-0.035 of each clay arm edge, rows 35-85 % of the sofa box; read with <aid>-lock.png

product_check.rule: each product inside its clay box +-15 % of the box size (<aid>-boxes.png); read visually
